title: Mission: reach a real person
drDigitalIntro:
Practice conversations are safe because nobody is on the other end. This one has somebody on the other end.
• Send one real message to somebody who will be glad to hear from you. That is the point of the whole unit.
• You will also take a screenshot — a picture of your own screen — and hand it to this page, which reads its size and shape to confirm you made it just now.
• The picture is measured on your own computer and never sent anywhere.
• On a Mac, hold Shift and Command and press 3. On Windows, press the Windows key and Shift and S, then save the picture.

playgroundTask.goal: You reached a real person and made a real screenshot

steps.say: Send one real message to somebody who will be pleased to hear from you.
steps.detail: It does not need to be an occasion. 'Thinking of you' is a complete message and always lands well.

steps.say: React to something they sent instead of typing a reply.
steps.detail: Press and hold the message, or double-tap it. A reaction says 'I read this' without either of you having to keep the conversation going.

steps.say: Take a screenshot of your screen right now, then pick it here.
steps.detail: A screenshot is a photograph of your own screen, saved as a picture file — usually onto your desktop or into Pictures. It is how you show somebody what you are seeing when describing it is hopeless.

steps.say: Start a video call and find the mute button before you need it.
steps.detail: Find mute and camera-off in the first ten seconds of a call, while nothing is urgent. Hunting for mute with a barking dog in the room is not the moment to learn where it lives.

drDigitalSuccess: A real message to a real person, and a screenshot you made yourself. Both of those are worth more than any practice conversation.
drDigitalHint: For the screenshot step, the picture has to be one you made in the last half hour — an old photo will be turned down, and the page will tell you how old it is.
